claim: Post-training ternarization (1.58-bit) with asymmetric ternary quantization and structural similarity-based reordering achieves competitive accuracy while reducing model size and accelerating inference compared to 2-bit quantization methods.
falsifier: The claim can be tested by applying the described asymmetric ternary quantizer and structural similarity reordering to other LLMs and measuring throughput, model size, and accuracy against 2-bit baselines under controlled memory budgets.

exclusions: Evidence is limited to the reported LLM architectures (LLaMA-65B), tasks (zero-shot QA), and quantization configurations; transfer beyond these is unestablished.
